gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't leave until the lights are off,' the caretaker begged us. The caretaker begged ___ until the lights were off.
gaps.explanation: Begging somebody not to do something uses object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'You should get a second opinion,' the doctor said. The doctor ___ a second opinion.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the reporting verb that takes object + to-infinitive; suggest and offer do not.

gaps.sentence: 'How long have you worked here?' she asked him. She asked him how long he ___ there.
gaps.explanation: have worked → had worked; 'here' becomes 'there' in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Could you open the window?' she asked. She asked me ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Could you...?' requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive; no could remains.
